articles.headline: NFL fines 49ers' Kyle Juszczyk for imitating 'chugging a beer'
articles.description: The NFL fined San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk $14,926 on Thursday for "engaging in offensive demonstrations."
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The NFL fined San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk $14,926 on Thursday for "engaging in offensive demonstrations."

According to the league, Juszczyk violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, when he did an "imitation of chugging a beer" with just under eight minutes left in the third quarter of the Niners' win against the Miami Dolphins. 

The fine notice went on to say that "players are expected to conduct themselves in a manner that reflects positively on the game and is consistent with NFL standards of sportsmanship." It added that further offenses will result in an escalation of disciplinary action, up to and including suspension. 

Juszczyk has already appealed the fine, he told ESPN's Adam Schefter. Juszczyk, who goes by the nickname "Juice," has done the celebration for years and has said that he's drinking his "juice" when asked about it. He has never been fined previously for the celebration and told Schefter via text that, "I don't even drink beer." 

In a post to X written Thursday morning in response to the fine, Juszczyk wrote, simply "Can't make this stuff up..." 

Juszczyk is in his 10th season with the 49ers after signing as a free agent from the Baltimore Ravens in 2017.

articles.headline: Udinese sign former Real Madrid defender David Alaba
articles.description: Former Real Madrid defender David Alaba officially signed for Serie A side Udinese on Thursday.
articles.body:
Former Real Madrid defender David Alaba officially signed for Serie A side Udinese on Thursday.

The 34-year-old has been a free agent since his contract with Real Madrid expired at the end of last season.

He spent five years with the LaLiga giants, winning 11 trophies including two Champions Leagues, two league titles and two FIFA Club World Cups.

"Signing David Alaba is a source of immense satisfaction for the entire club," GM Franco Collavino said in a news release. "We are welcoming an established champion, a leader and an exemplary professional. His arrival shows Udinese's determination to grow and compete at the highest level as well as build an increasingly ambitious squad."

The defender suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament injury in 2023 which required surgery and his minutes became limited.

Alaba had also previously spent 13 years with German club Bayern Munich, where he won 10 Bundesliga titles and two Champions Leagues.

"I've had many experiences and won a lot over the course of my career, but one thing hasn't changed, I still want to win," Alaba said in the Serie A club's news release. "I still want to compete. And I still want to achieve something special. That is the mindset I'm bringing to Udinese.

"The coach [Kosta Runjaić] made it very clear what role he has in mind for me and what he wants us to achieve together. Naturally, I want to bring my experience to the dressing room, take on responsibility, and help out whenever possible, especially with the younger players.

"I'm not coming here just to be the veteran of the squad, and I certainly didn't come here to wind down my career. I'm still too ambitious for that, and I still strongly believe in what I can do on the pitch. 

"I want to keep pushing, perform at the highest level in Serie A week in and week out, and achieve something meaningful. I'm really excited about this challenge, and I still have a lot to prove to myself."

Alaba has also made 117 appearances for his country, Austria, and captained the side at the World Cup this summer.

Udinese are currently 13th in the Serie A table with four points after five games, and have lost their last three.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Former England forward Andy Carroll says he was sexually assaulted by a man in 2021
articles.description: Former England forward Andy Carroll has revealed in his autobiography he was sexually assaulted by a man during 2021.
articles.body:
Former England forward Andy Carroll has said in his autobiography he was sexually assaulted by a man during 2021.

The 37-year-old included the details in his book, titled "Owning It." As a victim of sexual assault, Carroll was automatically granted anonymity.

Carroll said the incident took place at his home during a second spell at Newcastle. The offender -- a friend of his former partner, who was staying away at the time -- was later jailed for three years, with Carroll having testified in court.

Former Liverpool and West Ham striker Carroll, who is now a player/co-owner of National League South club Dagenham & Redbridge, said the incident happened when he was sleeping. He said he then threw the man out of the house, and knocked him unconscious when he attempted to get back inside.

"I was sexually assaulted, there I said it. Scary to even think about and only a few people knew about it before now," wrote Carroll, who had decided to include the incident in his book "at the very last minute" after discussing it with his girlfriend, Lou Teasdale.

"Me and Lou spent a lot of time discussing whether to mention it in this book or not. I avoided my publisher for so long that they probably suspected I got cold feet.

"Scary to talk about but it's made [me] the person I am today as much as any of the good stuff. And if me talking about it helps just one person then good, it will have been worth it."

Carroll said testifying in court, where the attacker was found guilty of sexual offences and placed on the sex offender register, was "humiliating and embarrassing and absolutely horrendous."

The 37-year-old said: "What happened to me affected every facet of my life. I'd think about it every day, making it difficult to focus on anything else, including football ... The trauma of what happened to me hasn't gone away."

articles.headline: Kyler Murray returns for the Vikings against the struggling Buccaneers
articles.description: — Kyler Murray has the right opponent to get back on track after a concussion knocked him out of the season opener.
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- — Kyler Murray has the right opponent to get back on track after a concussion knocked him out of the season opener.


              Murray will be under center when the Minnesota Vikings (2-0) visit the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-2) on Sunday. The two-time Pro Bowl quarterback faces a defense that made Deshaun Watson look like an elite quarterback last week.


              The Buccaneers haven’t generated much pressure, can’t tackle and routinely miss coverage assignments.


              That bodes well for Murray, who watched Carson Wentz fill in and lead Minnesota to two gritty wins. Wentz didn’t turn the ball over and made enough plays, especially in Week 1 when he tossed three touchdown passes against Green Bay.


              “I think the starting point is he’s just watched Carson really function in a way that Carson wasn’t doing crazy things,” Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said. “He was just protecting the football, making good decisions, making some big-time throws when he could and running the show. And I think he saw some plays get made. I think he saw our team play totally connected and complementary of the other two phases and what that can do for the Minnesota Vikings on a Sunday.”


              Wentz was sacked six times in the first two games, but Murray’s mobility can create problems for Tampa Bay.


              “It’s been a long time since (the) Arizona days, but he’s very good,” Bucs coach Todd Bowles said of Murray. “He has a very good arm – he can throw a deep ball. He’s very good in the pocket, throwing on a dime, and he can run with the ball. His feet are probably faster than our four defensive linemen’s feet, so we’ve got to be very disciplined in our pass rush.”


              Bowles already was on the hot seat after a 6-2 start in 2025 turned into an 8-9 finish. Now, the Bucs are 0-2 for the first time in 12 years. Baker Mayfield signed the biggest contract in franchise history and has more turnovers (four) than TDs (two). Defensive tackle Vita Vea got a huge contract extension and isn’t playing up to standards. Rookie edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr., a first-round draft pick with high expectations, hasn’t made an impact.


              “The urgency is every week. It just happens to be this week,” Bowles said. “We treat every week the same, with the same amount of urgency. The fact that it’s this week (means) it’s the most important game, and then next week will be the most important, and it’ll go from there.”


              Need to know
              Minnesota (2-0) at Tampa Bay (0-2).


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 4:05 p.m. EDT, Fox.


              Latest odds: Vikings by 1 1/2.


              Against the spread: Vikings 2-0; Buccaneers 0-2.


              Last week: Vikings beat the Bears 9-3; Buccaneers lost to the Browns 23-19.


              Last meeting: Buccaneers beat the Vikings 20-17 on Sept. 10, 2023, in Minnesota.


              Series record: Vikings lead

articles.headline: NBA Rank 2026: The new top 10 features a razor-thin race for No. 1
articles.description: Our countdown of the NBA's top 100 players hits its grand finale.
articles.body:
Welcome to the grand finale of NBA Rank 2026.

After unveiling Nos. 100-51 on Tuesday and Nos. 50-11 on Wednesday, the big reveal is here.

Who will be the top 10 players for the 2026-27 season? How high did reigning Finals MVP Jalen Brunson climb? Did Victor Wembanyama just begin a LeBron James-esque run atop of the list?

While ESPN's latest top 10 -- er, full top 100 -- will surely spark debate, what can't be questioned is the remarkably tight race for this season's No. 1 spot. Just three voting points separated Nikola Jokic, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Wembanyama, with each superstar placing atop at least one of the seven panelists' individual rankings.

That panel has been overhauled for the 2026 edition. In previous seasons, more than 100 ESPN NBA insiders, reporters, editors and producers voted on thousands of possible player vs. player matchups to arrive at the final top-100 list.

That "wisdom of the crowd" approach has given way to the wisdom of seven NBA experts: ESPN's Ben Golliver, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Bobby Marks, Dave McMenamin, André Snellings and Matt "Stats" Williams. (The panelists' individual top-100 lists were combined to create our final rankings.)

Voting guidelines, however, remained unchanged. The panel was asked to rank players based on predicted contributions -- quality and quantity -- for the 2026-27 regular season only.

Let's get to the list -- the best of the best heading into the new NBA season.

Note: Signature stats provided by ESPN Research.

10. Donovan Mitchell

G | Cleveland Cavaliers

Age: 30

2025 NBA Rank: 15

Mitchell rises into the top 10 after leading the Cavaliers to the Eastern Conference finals last season, his first such appearance in his nine-year career. He has finished in the top seven in MVP voting in three of the past four seasons, and his ability to create off the dribble while using his shooting range to freeze defenders makes him the offensive force of the Cavs. Mitchell has been an All-Star in seven straight seasons, and he pairs with James Harden to give Cleveland one of the few backcourts where each starter boasts multiple All-NBA selections. 

Big question: Can Mitchell be the best player on a champion?

The Cavaliers start four All-Stars in Mitchell, Harden, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, but in the playoffs they will go only as far as Mitchell can lead them.

One of the ironies of Mitchell's first run to the conference finals was that he didn't play particularly well compared with past postseasons. In his six playoffs runs, from 2020 to 2025, Mitchell averaged 30.0 points per game with a player efficiency rating of 24.5. Last season, he averaged 26.0 points with a PER of just 18.6 (15.0 is considered average). The former version is absolutely good enough to carry the Cavs back to the Finals, especially if Mitchell sees a repeat performance from his teammates. -- André Snellings

articles.headline: Fantasy football: What to do with early-season disappointments like Loveland, Herbert and more
articles.description: Matt Bowen discusses players who have struggled early on and offers his level of concern.
articles.body:
After two weeks of the NFL season, we're starting to get a sense of player usage and offensive game plans. That matters in fantasy football. And there are players who are starting to ascend at a quick rate, carving out roles and finding their way into weekly fantasy lineups.

However, we're also seeing a group of players failing to meet those high preseason expectations, which can put managers in a tough spot this early in the season. It doesn't matter where you drafted them because the best managers are willing to make hard decisions to win.

That's what we are doing here today with seven players who are off to rocky starts. For some, you can ride it out: Move them down to the flex spot, roll the dice on big-play ability, etc. But for the others? It's time to sit them or cut them loose.

Let's get into it.

Justin Herbert, QB, Los Angeles Chargers

With a new offensive system under coordinator Mike McDaniel, I expected a lot more from Herbert to start this season given the home matchups in Weeks 1 and 2 (Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders, respectively).

However, Herbert is scoring just 10.3 fantasy PPG, while averaging 200.5 passing yards -- with two touchdown throws on the season -- and the rushing totals are down, too (eight carries, 31 yards). Plus, this L.A. passing game has been much more vertical than I expected, as Herbert's 10.3 air yards per target is the second highest in the league.

Now, the Chargers can (and will) make game-plan changes going forward, which could include more play-action throws (Herbert ranks 25th in play-action attempts) and moving the pocket to compensate for a struggling interior offensive line.

But if we do see growth in this Chargers offense, Herbert's upcoming schedule presents a tough stretch of matchups. Will we get a shootout-type game versus the Buffalo Bills in Week 3? Potentially. But I'm not willing to take that risk. With games in Weeks 4 and 5 against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos defenses, Herbert should be viewed as QB2 for now.

Colston Loveland, TE, Chicago Bears

Loveland has been absent from the Bears passing attack through two games, catching just one of five targets for three yards (1.3 fantasy points).

Despite the low volume, Loveland has 30.5 routes run per game (up from 23.8 in 2025), and his route tree has a lot of branches. Loveland is being deployed at all three levels of the field: verticals (27.5%), short out routes (19.6%), short in-breakers (15.7%), crossers (13.7%) and more. He's just not seeing the ball -- yet.

The Bears' uncertainty at quarterback for Week 3 versus the Philadelphia Eagles creates some concern. With Caleb Williams (hamstring) most likely out, I would still play Loveland as a TE1 if backup Tyson Bagent (concussion) is cleared. But if it gets to No. 3 Case Keenum? I might pivot to a streamer for this one game, and that's OK.
